families.name: Basics
families.blurb: Validate the workspace, the control cadence, and your recording pipeline before any object is involved.

families.name: Object manipulation
families.blurb: The best baseline family for most 6-DOF labs: grasp, transport, orient, and release rigid objects.

families.name: Surface cleaning
families.blurb: Force-aware trajectories and coverage. The arm stays in contact with a surface instead of moving through free space.

families.name: Laundry handling
families.blurb: Deformable state is only partly observable. Start with towels: forgiving, and the state change is visible.

families.name: Kitchen & table reset
families.blurb: The bridge from atomic skills to ordered, language-conditioned sequences.

families.name: Failure recovery
families.blurb: Detect, retreat, re-observe, retry within a budget, escalate. Generalization comes from a system, not a checkpoint.

families.name: Rigid objects
families.blurb: Real colliders: cubes and spheres with mass, friction, and gravity. The gripper only holds what is actually between its jaws, and whatever it lets go of falls, slides, or rolls.

workflows.name: Bin reach
workflows.instruction: Move the gripper above the amber marker and hold the pose.
workflows.summary: The calibration task. No grasp, no contact — just prove that the goal is reachable, the safety clamp holds, and an episode records cleanly.
workflows.success: End-effector within 20 mm of the marker for 10 consecutive control steps with every action inside the joint-delta cap.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB only. Joint encoders are the ground truth at this stage.
curriculum: Marker moved between four corners of the workspace
Marker sampled uniformly in the reachable set
Marker placed near the reach boundary so the projection clamp fires
failure_modes: Goal outside the reachable radius is silently projected — check the projection before blaming the policy
IK settles in a joint-limit local minimum from an operator-dragged pose
workflows.guardrail: Nothing enters the workspace during this task. It is the task you run after any change to limits, gearing, or the safety wrapper.

workflows.name: Pick & place
workflows.instruction: Approach the cube, close the gripper, then move it to the bin.
workflows.summary: The reference skill of the whole library. Everything downstream is pick-and-place with more state, more steps, or more contact.
workflows.success: Stable grasp held through transport, object released inside the bin footprint, and the arm retreats to a clear pose.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB to begin; add a wrist camera as soon as the gripper occludes the object.
curriculum: Cube position randomized in a 15 cm patch
failure_modes: Grasp closes early because the wrist camera is missing
Transport path clips the bin rim
Release happens before the object is over the bin
workflows.guardrail: Soft or light objects only. Set workspace, speed, and torque limits before a single demonstration is collected.

workflows.name: Part sorting
workflows.instruction: Move the part from the workcell into its designated lane.
workflows.summary: Pick-and-place plus a decision. The policy must read a visual property — colour, shape, label — and choose a destination from it.
workflows.success: Correct-lane rate above 90% on held-out part placements, with mis-sorts recoverable rather than jammed.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB for the class cue, wrist RGB for the grasp. Depth helps once parts overlap.
curriculum: Classes that differ by shape rather than colour
Parts presented in a cluttered pile
failure_modes: Policy memorizes position instead of the class cue — test by swapping lane assignments
Lighting change collapses the colour boundary
workflows.guardrail: Lanes must be physically separated so a mis-sort is a wrong bin, never a collision.

workflows.name: Cup stacking
workflows.instruction: Place the cup squarely on top of the stack without toppling it.
workflows.summary: The first task where the goal pose depends on what the arm did previously. Placement tolerance shrinks with every layer.
workflows.success: Three cups stacked and still standing five seconds after release; lateral offset under 8 mm per layer.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB + wrist RGB. A compliant gripper buys more tolerance than a better policy does.
curriculum: Place onto a fixed base cup
Base cup position randomized between layers
failure_modes: Release velocity topples the stack even though the pose was correct
Error accumulates across layers because each placement is scored independently
workflows.guardrail: Cap descent speed near contact. A stack collapse must not become a lateral sweep across the table.

workflows.name: Peg insertion
workflows.instruction: Align the peg with the hole and insert it without jamming.
workflows.summary: The canonical contact-rich task. Position control alone will jam; the policy has to learn the small corrective wiggle.
workflows.success: Full insertion depth reached with peak contact force under the configured limit, in under 15 seconds.
workflows.sensors: Wrist RGB plus force/torque. This is the first task where an F/T sensor stops being optional.
failure_modes: Jam detected as zero progress at high force — needs a retreat-and-retry, not more push
Multimodal corrective motions get averaged into nothing by a unimodal policy
workflows.guardrail: Force limiting belongs in the hardware wrapper, not in the learned policy. Insertion is the task most likely to damage a gearbox.

workflows.name: Surface wipe
workflows.instruction: Pick up the cloth, cover the marked spill area, then return the tool.
workflows.summary: Coverage rather than a single endpoint. The reward is spatial and the arm holds contact for the length of the episode.
workflows.success: Coverage of the marked area above 95%, tool returned to its holder, and the end-effector never crosses the table edge.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB for coverage scoring; a compliant end-effector or F/T sensor for contact.
curriculum: Dry wipe of a fixed rectangle
Visually marked spill of varying shape
Cluttered table with objects to avoid
failure_modes: Policy lifts off mid-stroke and coverage scoring silently keeps counting
Cloth slips in the gripper and the stroke continues on an empty tool
workflows.guardrail: Water only after electrical and slip hazards are controlled. Keep cleaning chemicals out of the training loop entirely.

workflows.name: Towel fold
workflows.instruction: Pin one edge with the left arm while the right arm lifts the opposite edge and folds it over.
workflows.summary: Deformable state you cannot fully observe, and the first task that genuinely needs two grippers: one arm holds the towel flat while the other folds. Towels are the entry point because the state change is large and visible from one camera.
workflows.success: Folded edge within 3 cm of the pinned edge, no snagging, and the towel still flat under the holding gripper.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB + a wrist camera per arm. Depth helps enormously in finding a liftable edge.
curriculum: Single fold from a flattened start
Fold from a lightly crumpled start
failure_modes: Gripper closes on two layers and the fold tears the stack apart
Edge detection succeeds but the lift angle drags the whole towel
workflows.guardrail: Keep the arm outside any appliance. Never automate a door, drum, or heat source without dedicated safety hardware.

workflows.name: Drawer opening
workflows.instruction: Grasp the handle, pull along the drawer axis, and release.
workflows.summary: An articulated object: the environment, not the policy, decides the trajectory. Off-axis force is the thing to measure.
workflows.success: Drawer opened at least 12 cm with off-axis force below the limit and the handle released cleanly.
workflows.sensors: Wrist RGB for the handle, F/T for the constraint. Joint effort is a usable proxy if there is no F/T sensor.
curriculum: Drawer at a fixed angle to the base
failure_modes: Arm fights the kinematic constraint and trips the effort limit
Grasp slips off a round handle under load
workflows.guardrail: Articulated objects must have a mechanical stop. Configure the effort limit below the point where the arm can move the furniture.

workflows.name: Table reset
workflows.instruction: Clear the left side to the tray while the right arm sorts the utensils into their zone.
workflows.summary: Multi-step, order-dependent, and split across two arms working the same table without colliding. This is where a language-conditioned policy starts earning its cost over a stack of specialists.
workflows.success: Every object reaches its correct zone in the required order, with no spills, collisions between the arms, or unsafe contact.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB + a wrist camera per arm. Markers or barcodes are a legitimate shortcut for the first datasets.
curriculum: Ordered reset with a required sequence
failure_modes: Policy completes steps in the wrong order and the tray is blocked
Long horizon drifts: early success, late-episode collapse
workflows.guardrail: No knives, hot surfaces, glass, liquids, or food-contact tasks until there is a reviewed safety case for the whole cell.

workflows.name: Safe handoff
workflows.instruction: Present the object with the left arm and take it with the right, then release.
workflows.summary: An arm-to-arm handoff: the release of one gripper has to be conditioned on the grasp of the other. The interesting behaviour is the waiting, not the reaching. The same contract covers a handoff to a person, where the second arm is replaced by a hand and the safety case gets much larger.
workflows.success: Object transferred with both grippers closed on it for at least 10 control steps, then a clean release and retreat by the presenting arm.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB, both gripper states, and — for a human receiver — a presence channel that is not the learned policy’s to interpret.
failure_modes: Policy releases on visual similarity rather than the signal
Arm keeps tracking a receding hand outside the safe zone
workflows.guardrail: Human-adjacent operation needs a speed and separation monitor, a dead-man control, and a physical e-stop. The browser lab cannot model any of them.

workflows.name: Failure recovery
workflows.instruction: Detect the dropped object, retreat, re-observe, and attempt one safe retry.
workflows.summary: Not a manipulation skill — a system skill. The measurable outcome is what happens after something goes wrong.
workflows.success: Robot halts safely, classifies the failure, and either completes or escalates within a bounded retry budget.
workflows.sensors: The task cameras plus gripper state, joint effort, and an explicit stop channel independent of the policy.
failure_modes: Retry loop with no budget becomes an unbounded hammering motion
Failure classified as success because the reward only reads the final pose
workflows.guardrail: Every learned policy needs a deterministic stop, a retreat pose, and a human takeover path. Build this before the policy that needs it.

workflows.name: Configurable fold
workflows.instruction: Choose which corner each gripper grasps, preview the fold line, then fold.
workflows.summary: Task 07's fold with the grasp point exposed as a setting instead of fixed: each arm grasps either its true front corner or one vertex in from it, and a preview line shows the resulting fold direction before the policy runs. The safe range is narrow - the arm reach that makes Task 07's pair comfortable does not extend to the towel's back corners or to swapped roles, both of which fail the same safety check a live run would.
workflows.success: Folded edge within 3 cm of the pinned edge, no snagging, and the towel still flat under the holding gripper, for whichever grasp vertices were selected.
workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB + a wrist camera per arm. Depth helps enormously in finding a liftable edge.
curriculum: True-corner grasp on both sides (Task 07's exact case)
One vertex inset on the carried side only
One vertex inset on the pinned side only
Preview the fold line before committing to a run
failure_modes: A requested grasp vertex the arm cannot safely reach is rejected before any motion, not discovered mid-fold
Gripper closes on two layers and the fold tears the stack apart
workflows.guardrail: Keep the arm outside any appliance. Never automate a door, drum, or heat source without dedicated safety hardware.

workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB for the object pose; joint encoders plus a gripper width reading tell a real grasp from an empty close.
workflows.guardrail: Light, blunt objects only while grasp and release are being tuned. A dropped part is data, not a failure to hide - log it.
workflows.name: Cube pick & place
workflows.instruction: Pick up the green cube and set it down inside the marked square.
workflows.summary: The first task with a real rigid body. The cube has mass and friction, the gripper's fingers are colliders, and nothing is attached by proximity: a top-down grasp has to straddle the cube, and a release anywhere but the table leaves it to fall.
workflows.success: Cube center inside the 50 mm square, flat on the table, not held, and at rest.
curriculum: Cube yawed so the jaws close across a diagonal
Zone moved by clicking the scene
Cube nudged after planning, so the grasp misses and the run is scored a failure
failure_modes: Grasp planned on a stale object pose closes on air - the jaws only hold what is between them
A release too high lets the cube bounce out of the zone

workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB for the object pose; joint encoders plus a gripper width reading tell a real grasp from an empty close.
workflows.guardrail: Light, blunt objects only while grasp and release are being tuned. A dropped part is data, not a failure to hide - log it.
workflows.name: Ball into tray
workflows.instruction: Pick up the ball and drop it into the tray.
workflows.summary: A sphere has one contact point with the table and nothing stops it rolling, so it is unforgiving of a sloppy release. The tray's walls are real colliders too: a ball dropped inside stays inside, and one that clips a wall bounces off it.
workflows.success: Ball center inside the tray's walls, below their rim, not held, and at rest.
curriculum: Release just above the tray floor
Release from higher up - the walls have to catch it
Tray moved by clicking the scene
failure_modes: Ball squeezed off-center rolls out of the jaws
A release with any sideways tool velocity sends the ball rolling

workflows.sensors: Overhead RGB for the object pose; joint encoders plus a gripper width reading tell a real grasp from an empty close.
workflows.guardrail: Light, blunt objects only while grasp and release are being tuned. A dropped part is data, not a failure to hide - log it.
workflows.name: Cube stack
workflows.instruction: Stack the green cube squarely on the blue one.
workflows.summary: Two free cubes. The carried cube is still a collider while held, so it lands on the base cube instead of passing through it, and the base cube is free to be knocked over by a careless placement.
workflows.success: Top cube resting on the base cube within 8 mm of centered, base cube not pushed more than 15 mm, both at rest.
curriculum: Base cube square to the table edge
Top cube yawed relative to the base
Base cube moved - the plan reads its live pose
failure_modes: Placing with a sideways velocity shoves the base cube off its spot
Releasing too high tips the top cube off the edge

models.name: ACT
models.use: Fast, task-specific imitation baseline for a fixed workcell. The dependable first learned policy for short, well-scoped, teleoperated skills.

models.name: Diffusion Policy
models.use: Generates action sequences by denoising. A strong fit for multimodal, contact-rich motion such as insertion, folding, and wiping.

models.name: SmolVLA
models.use: Fine-tunable open vision-language-action policy for camera-guided, SO-101-style manipulation when compute and data are constrained.

models.name: OpenVLA
models.use: Open 7B vision-language-action model for generalist manipulation. Fine-tune it when instructions, visual variation, and broad task coverage matter.

models.name: π₀ / π₀.₅
models.use: Flow-based generalist robot policies from Physical Intelligence. A reference point for open-world, long-horizon, multi-task robot learning.

models.name: GR00T N1.x
models.use: NVIDIA's open robot foundation-model family, paired with Isaac data and simulation tooling. Strongest fit when the Isaac ecosystem is already in play.

datasets.name: LeRobotDataset recordings
datasets.purpose: Teleoperation, camera frames, state/action and task text for the specific workcell.

datasets.name: SVLA SO-101 pick-place
datasets.purpose: Example dataset and task setup for SmolVLA fine-tuning and real SO-101 pick-and-place.

datasets.name: Open X-Embodiment
datasets.purpose: Cross-embodiment demonstrations used to pretrain generalist policies before task-specific fine-tuning.

datasets.name: DROID
datasets.purpose: Large in-the-wild manipulation dataset collected across many scenes and operators.

datasets.name: RoboCasa / LIBERO
datasets.purpose: Held-out scene and task evaluation before considering hardware deployment.
